doc.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017

title: Valery Ponomarev and the NJPAC teens: the future of jazz
summary: Seeing teens play jazz convinces him jazz has a future, though never popular as in the 30s and 40s.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Can you tell me what MJPAC is?

They have a thing called jazz for teens. And they have these kids come in, and he is instructing them how to play jazz. And man these kids, I mean they couldn’t have been any more than maybe 14, 15. And the trumpeter was cool. He was the leader, because he had on the nice suit and the nice shiny shoes and the little handkerchief in his pocket and had his hair all slicked back, had his horn. And he was leading them man. I mean and they’re playing “Night in Tunisia,” the drummer’s doing the thing, and Valery is sitting next to me and he’s just laughing his butt off. “Listen to that, the phrase, they’re answering each other.” The pianist is answering the guy that was playing the sax. And you see that and you say, “Okay. There’s a future. That’s the future. These kids know man.” They’ve obviously been listening and they’ve been picking it up, and people like

Valery is hipping them and so I think jazz is going to be okay. It’s never going to be popular like it was in the 30s and 40s. You’re never going to see that again. That’s gone, that’s done. But it’s going to be there. If you want to see it, and you know where to find it, you will find it, because it will be there. And we have all these programs still, you have all these colleges with jazz happening in them. You have master’s degrees in jazz history now so that those people will be out there. So I think it’s in good hands. It just isn’t going to be like it was in the old days. I also think that you can always find the kind of jazz you’re really interested in. Someone’s playing it somewhere. If you like Dixieland you can find it. There’s somebody somewhere doing it. Somebody just told me that there seems to be this now growth in swing bands, like small swing bands, people playing that type of music now more than they did before. And maybe that’s happening. That’s great. I think the jazz parties are dying though. I don’t think you’ll have too many more of those anymore.
